walkthroughs.body_html: Cortés landed at what became Veracruz in April 1519 with about 500 men, 16 horses and 14 cannon. He famously scuttled his ships to prevent retreat. Through diplomacy, force and the interpreting skills of La Malinche, he gathered Indigenous allies — most importantly the Tlaxcalans — and approached the imperial capital.

The Spaniards entered Tenochtitlán on 8 November 1519, marvelling at the lake-city of perhaps 200,000 inhabitants. Moctezuma was effectively held captive. Tensions exploded during Pedro de Alvarado's massacre at the Templo Mayor; the Spaniards barely escaped on the Noche Triste of 30 June - 1 July 1520.

Smallpox tore through the Aztec population, killing the new emperor Cuitláhuac. Cortés regrouped, built brigantines on Lake Texcoco and besieged the capital. Tenochtitlán fell on 13 August 1521 with the capture of Cuauhtémoc. Mexico-Tenochtitlán became the foundation of the viceroyalty of New Spain.
